# Secrets and Configuration (SEC)

## SCS-SEC-01 Never hardcode or commit secrets

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Credentials, API keys, tokens, connection strings, certificates, private keys and signing keystores MUST NEVER be hardcoded in source code or committed to Git, in any repository, including internal ones. Any secret that has been committed, logged or shipped MUST be rotated immediately; deleting it from the file is not enough.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Add .env, *.pfx, *.p12, *.jks, *.keystore, key.properties, secrets.json and appsettings.*.local.json to .gitignore in every repository.
- Run a secret scanner as a pre-commit hook and in CI (for example gitleaks); see SCS-SEC-03.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Never put secrets in appsettings.json or appsettings.{Environment}.json that are committed.
- Never send secrets in URLs (?key=...); query strings end up in logs.

Verification: gitleaks (or equivalent) scan of the full history is clean. Grep for Password=, ApiKey, Secret, -----BEGIN, AIza in source.

Current gap: IT-57 §11 #4 records pre-commit secret scanning hooks as planned.

## SCS-SEC-02 Load secrets from secure configuration and validate them at startup

Level: MUST

Applies to: Backend (.NET / SQL Server)

Policy: Secrets MUST come from Azure Key Vault or environment variables in staging and production, and from .NET User Secrets on developer machines. appsettings.json holds non-sensitive settings only. The application MUST validate required settings at startup and refuse to start if one is missing or malformed.

Implementation (.NET / SQL Server):

- Precedence (highest first): command line > environment variables > User Secrets (Development only) > appsettings.{Environment}.json > appsettings.json.
- Production: builder.Configuration.AddAzureKeyVault(vaultUri, new DefaultAzureCredential()) with managed identity, or environment variables (Section__Key) set by the deployment.
- Development: dotnet user-secrets (stored unencrypted in the user profile, so never use real production secrets there).
- Validate options: AddOptions<T>().BindConfiguration("Section").ValidateDataAnnotations().ValidateOnStart().
- If DotNetEnv is used for local .env files: Env.NoClobber().Load() (the default overwrites real environment variables), on developer machines only, and keep .env out of Git and out of publish output.
- Each secret has an owner and a documented rotation path; record where each value lives in the application's CONFIGURATION.md.

Verification: Start the app with a required secret missing and confirm it fails at startup. Review appsettings*.json for secrets.

## SCS-SEC-03 Scan for secrets before every commit and in CI

Level: SHOULD

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every repository SHOULD run an automated secret scanner as a Git pre-commit hook and in the CI pipeline, so that secrets are blocked before they reach the remote repository.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Install gitleaks (or detect-secrets) and add it as a pre-commit hook (for example via the pre-commit framework or a Husky/Lefthook hook).
- Run the same scanner in the pipeline on every merge request; a finding fails the build.
- Turn on the Git hosting platform's secret scanning / push protection where available.

Verification: Commit a dummy test secret in a sandbox branch and confirm the hook blocks it.

Current gap: IT-57 §11 #4 records pre-commit hooks as planned. This becomes MUST once the hooks are rolled out.
